assessment: Four wishes in the 99, and every one is a road to the same city: Aggravated Assault plus a connecting Dragon. Two tutors deliver to hand (Sarkhan's Triumph, Tiamat) and two deliver to the top of your library (Enlightened Tutor, Worldly Tutor) — schedule the top-deckers a turn ahead, and remember that Korlessa, Scale Singer and Herald's Horn both convert 'on top' into 'castable' or 'in hand'. Every fetch is revealed, so a wish is also an announcement: buy the kill piece the turn before you use it, not earlier. One funding law governs everything — the five spells-only sources (Haven of the Spirit Dragon, Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon, Unclaimed Territory, Rivaz of the Claw, Klauth) can pay for the tutors themselves, because tutors are spells, but never for Assault's {3}{R}{R} activation. Treasures and lands close the game; restricted mana only shops for it.

targets.scenario: End of the turn before your pivot: Old Gnawbone or Savage Ventmaw is on board, Treasures or five untapped lands are ready, and your hand holds no win button.
targets.why: One mana buys the combo exit. Draw it next turn, cast it, and you are inside the verified kill: Ventmaw self-funds at +1 mana per cycle (stack 003), and Gnawbone banks net +2 Treasures per unblocked cycle and kills the table sequentially (stack 006). Fund the {3}{R}{R} with Treasures or lands — the spells-only sources never pay an activation. The reveal announces the kill, so buy it the turn before you win, not two.

targets.scenario: Turn 2-3, hand full of six- and seven-drops, no cost reducer in sight.
targets.why: The goldfish calls cost reducers the deck's real curve fixer and says one is drawn by turn 6 in only 33.2% of games. Incubator plus eminence takes {3} off every Dragon — the top shelf becomes castable turns early. One mana to fix the deck's rarest resource is the best behind-fetch in the book.

targets.scenario: Mid-game, a payoff (Dragon Tempest, Terror of the Peaks, Scourge of Valkas) already down, expensive Dragons stranded in hand.
targets.why: {R} per Dragon, haste, every enters- and attacks-trigger live, and the damage stands after the end-step sacrifice — stack 005 verified the rate at one {R} for Drakuseth's 17. As an enchantment it also shrugs off the wraths pointed at your creatures.

targets.scenario: Miirym is on board and holding; the table believes it has priced your doubling.
targets.why: Nobody plays around the artifact. Stack 002 verified the cascade: with Miirym, Panharmonicon, Terror of the Peaks, and Dragon Tempest down, one Lathliss cast produced two extra Lathlisses and 64 damage across twelve targeted triggers. The quiet fetch that turns your next Dragon into a table-shaking event.

tutors.notes: Enlightened tops the library — it costs you the draw step, so cast it at the end of the turn before you want the card. The reveal is public: fetching Aggravated Assault tells every bracket-4 player exactly what is coming, so pair the wish with held protection (Deflecting Swat is the bodyguard).

targets.scenario: Aggravated Assault is on board or in hand, the Treasure funding exists, and you need the other half tonight.
targets.why: Instant speed, to hand, one cast from the verified table-kill: Gnawbone plus Assault banks net +2 Treasures per unblocked cycle and kills opponents sequentially — combats 6 and 12 in the verified game (stack 006). Gnawbone's own Treasures pay every activation, which matters because your spells-only mana never can.

targets.scenario: Assault is live but your mana is stretched — you can cast one Dragon this turn and not much more.
targets.why: The cheaper engine half, and the self-funding one: Ventmaw's attack trigger adds {R}{R}{R}{G}{G}{G}, which pays the {3}{R}{R} with {R} left over — +1 mana per cycle, verified in stack 003. You need exactly one clean combat; the loop pays for itself after that.

targets.scenario: You expect a damage-based sweeper next rotation — or you are holding Blasphemous Act yourself.
targets.why: Cast him ahead of the sweep and the sweeper becomes a trap: stack 004 verified Blasphemous Act into three of your Dragons throwing 39 at one opponent's face, the triggers resolving from beyond the grave. Know the boundary — destroy-all and exile-all effects deal no damage and feed him nothing. The instant-speed Sneak Attack ambush version is a candidate that still needs a stack scenario; do not bank on it.

targets.scenario: The table is playing around a nine-mana commander (goldfish mean cast 8.967) — and you would rather not pay it at all.
targets.why: The deck's real commander cheat, named by stack 005's refutation: Courser's enters-trigger puts The Ur-Dragon onto the battlefield from the command zone with haste for one attack — a card per attacking Dragon, a free permanent from hand, and he goes home at end step with no tax accrued. Nobody sees a mid-priced 6/6 coming with a nine-drop in its pocket.

tutors.notes: Dragon creature cards only — Triumph cannot find Assault, Sneak Attack, or any artifact. Three mana at instant speed means you shop on an opponent's end step and keep your whole turn for the cast.

targets.scenario: The standard cast, turn 6-8: eminence brings Tiamat down a mana, the board is stable, and you are shopping for the endgame. The default package is five names: Old Gnawbone, Savage Ventmaw, Miirym, Sentinel Wyrm, Dragonlord Kolaghan, Hellkite Courser.
targets.why: Every seat earns its keep. Gnawbone and Ventmaw are both Assault partners — the verified table-kill and the self-funding loop (stacks 006 and 003) — so whichever half you draw completes a kill. Miirym doubles every Dragon that follows (stack 002). Kolaghan hastes the whole wave so it attacks the turn it lands. Courser rents The Ur-Dragon for a draw-two-plus-free-permanent attack with no tax (stack 005's refutation names him the real commander cheat). One resolved Tiamat hands you both engine bodies, the multiplier, the haste anthem, and the commander — the rest of the game in one search.

targets.scenario: Against the wall: board swept, life pressured, the table ahead on tempo. The wall package: Dragonlord Dromoka, Wrathful Red Dragon, Atsushi, the Blazing Sky, Goldspan Dragon, Drakuseth, Maw of Flames.
targets.why: This pile trades speed for certainty. Dromoka is uncounterable, gains you life, and locks opponents out of casting spells on your turn — your rebuild resolves in peace. Wrathful makes every damage sweeper a 39-point mistake (stack 004). Atsushi dies forward into three unrestricted Treasures — Assault money — or two impulse cards. Goldspan brings haste, a Treasure per attack, and doubles every Treasure's value. Drakuseth is the removal spell that attacks: 10 damage split three ways before blockers (stack 005 shows his rate). Every body defends, refunds, or removes — you climb back on cards that cannot lose you more ground.

tutors.notes: Two laws. Tiamat's trigger reads 'if you cast it' — a Sneak Attack'd Tiamat or a Miirym copy searches for nothing, so Tiamat is the one Dragon you always hard-cast. And the five must be Dragon cards with different names, none of them Tiamat.

targets.scenario: Turn 3-4, one green open at an opponent's end step; the engine wants its multiplier.
targets.why: The doubler comes first: every nontoken Dragon after Miirym arrives twice, and under Panharmonicon he triggers twice per Dragon (stack 002). With Korlessa, Scale Singer on board, 'on top' already means 'castable' — the wish skips your hand entirely.

targets.scenario: Aggravated Assault is on board with Treasures or lands ready to pay {3}{R}{R} after your next draw.
targets.why: One green at instant speed sets up the verified table-kill: draw Gnawbone, cast him, connect once, and the engine banks net +2 Treasures per cycle while opponents die sequentially (stack 006). No other one-mana spell in the deck buys a whole endgame.

targets.scenario: Sneak Attack is down, a payoff is out, and you need damage now, not development.
targets.why: Stack 005 verified the exchange rate: {R} puts Drakuseth in with haste, and 17 damage — 4 plus 3 plus 3 from the trigger, 7 more in combat — stands after the end-step sacrifice. Worldly turns any topdeck into that line for one green mana.

tutors.notes: The wish is revealed and it sits on top, so time it. With Herald's Horn out, the upkeep peek puts a topped Dragon straight into your hand for free; with Korlessa, you cast it off the library. Cast Worldly at the last legal moment so the table prices your draw step wrong.

gaps: No tutor reaches the graveyard — Patriarch's Bidding is a mass rebuy, not a search. Once a key Dragon is exiled, no wish recovers it.

Enlightened Tutor is the only search that finds Aggravated Assault, and all three contained infinites route through that one enchantment (deck-facts). One tutor's worth of redundancy is thin cover for the deck's single point of failure — land the wish with protection held.
The Cavern-Hoard Dragon plus Assault pairing is a candidate that needs a stack scenario, so no wish here banks on it — fetch Gnawbone or Ventmaw, the verified halves (stacks 006, 003).
Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon's sacrifice mode tutors a Dragon to hand, but it is a land — its story belongs to Sources Say, not Fetch Quests.
